documents.title: Guidelines for the Use of Generative AI
documents.stance_why: The document sets no rule on whether students may use AI: it says 'Faculty should be clear with students ... about their policies on permitted uses, if any' and tells students to ask instructors, so the decision goes to instructors.
documents.summary: Library and IT guidelines from August 2024 mainly about data protection, output review and phishing risk. On classroom use it only asks faculty to tell students their policy and students to ask.

units.why: The opening sentence sets the purpose and scope of the guidance: 'set forth guidance for the appropriate use of generative AI tools at Bucknell'. It is an institution-level framework statement, so P56 fits (general, informs).
units.anchor: These guidelines set forth guidance for the appropriate use of generative AI tools at Bucknell.

units.why: The definition 'Generative AI refers to a type of artificial intelligence that utilizes deep-learning models' fixes what the guidelines cover, which is P61 (definition and scope), general, informs.
units.anchor: Generative AI refers to a type of artificial intelligence that utilizes deep-learning models

units.why: 'No Generative AI tool meets the University's security, privacy, and compliance standards for handling anything besides publicly available information' is a statement about which data tools may handle; it is data protection and tool vetting (P50), informs, and restricts what may be entered.
units.anchor: No Generative AI tool meets the University's security, privacy, and compliance standards

units.why: 'You should never enter any institutional data or information protected by the Family Education Rights and Privacy Act (FERPA)' is a prohibition on entering protected data, addressed to everyone; P50 (protect confidential data) fits better than P49 because it concerns institutional and FERPA data, not course materials.
units.anchor: You should never enter any institutional data or information protected by the Family

units.why: 'Entering data into a Generative AI tool or service is like posting that data on a public website' explains why privacy matters; a factual warning under P50 (tools store prompts), informs.
units.anchor: Entering data into a Generative AI tool or service is like posting that data

units.why: 'Any data you enter into a Generative AI tool becomes part of its training data' states a fact about data retention and exposure; it is the P50 rationale (tools store prompts), informs.
units.anchor: Any data you enter into a Generative AI tool becomes part of its training data

units.why: 'Generative AI content can be inaccurate, misleading, or entirely fabricated' warns of hallucinations, the core of P31 (AI output is often wrong), informs.
units.anchor: Generative AI content can be inaccurate, misleading, or entirely fabricated

units.why: 'may contain copyrighted material' flags the copyright risk of AI output, which is P52 (licensing and copyright of output), informs.
units.anchor: or may contain copyrighted material

units.why: 'Generative AI material may exhibit biases and discriminatory ideas or content' names bias as a harm; P53 (bias, harms), informs.
units.anchor: Generative AI material may exhibit biases and discriminatory ideas or content.

units.why: 'You are responsible for any content that you produce or publish that includes Generative AI material' makes the user accountable for what they submit or publish, so P29 (own what you submit), must, addressed to all.
units.anchor: You are responsible for any content that you produce or publish that includes

units.why: 'You should review all outputs from Generative AI for accuracy, including spot-checking of sources or facts, and bias' tells users to verify output, which is P31, should.
units.anchor: You should review all outputs from Generative AI for accuracy

units.why: 'Faculty should be clear with students ... about their policies on permitted uses, if any, of Generative AI' asks instructors to communicate expectations, which is P09 (state AI expectations); instructor, course-start, should.
units.anchor: Faculty should be clear with students they are teaching and advising about their policies

units.why: The same sentence leaves 'permitted uses, if any' to each faculty member's own policy; the university sets no rule and delegates, so P04 (each instructor sets the rule). The communication duty in the previous unit is coded P09; this unit captures the delegation.
units.anchor: policies on permitted uses, if any, of Generative AI in classes and on academic work
units.policy: Faculty decide whether and how generative AI may be used in their classes and on academic work.

units.why: 'Students are also encouraged to ask their instructors for clarification about these policies as needed' is the ask-first advice, P10, student, should.
units.anchor: Students are also encouraged to ask their instructors for clarification about these policies as needed.

units.why: 'Generative AI has made it easier for malicious actors to create sophisticated phishing emails and deepfakes' with advice to follow security practices and report suspicious messages; this is a security-awareness rule that is not about teaching or personal data protection and fits no listed type.
units.anchor: report suspicious messages to techdesk@bucknell.edu
units.uncovered_note: Guidance to stay alert to AI-enabled phishing and deepfakes and to report suspicious messages to IT (security awareness).

documents.title: WAC Council Statement on the Use of Generative AI in W Courses
documents.stance_why: For W courses the document says 'all W courses will emphasize and assign writing to be completed without genAI use' and recommends no genAI at all in W1s; AI is excluded from the writing process, with uses elsewhere not addressed, so restrict.
documents.summary: WAC Council statement (October 2025) for writing-designated courses. W courses should assign writing completed without genAI; W1 should permit none in the writing process; W2 needs at least one assignment without genAI.

units.why: The Council 'finds the use of generative AI ... in W courses to be incompatible with the Program's aims': a reasoned position that AI in the writing process undermines what W courses are for, so P41 (AI shortcuts the practice that builds skill); general, informs, and the position restricts AI.
units.anchor: to be incompatible with the Program's aims.

units.why: 'Given the importance of writing as a tool for thinking and learning and of writing as a process' gives the reason for limiting AI: the writing process itself builds knowledge; P41, informs.
units.anchor: importance of writing as a tool for thinking and learning

units.why: 'The WAC Council expects that all W courses will emphasize and assign writing to be completed without genAI use' sets the default for the covered courses: no AI on writing assignments. P01 (prohibit by default); instructors are the actors, 'expects' gives should.
units.anchor: all W courses will emphasize and assign writing to be completed without genAI use

units.why: 'We recommend that genAI use not be permitted at all in students' writing processes in W1s' is a firm recommendation of a ban in W1 courses. P01 fits; P08 (staging by level) is not chosen because it is a ban, with the W2 level in a separate unit.
units.anchor: genAI use not be permitted at all in students' writing processes in W1s.

units.why: 'W2 courses must include at least one writing assignment or project that requires students to plan, compose, revise (with human feedback) and edit a draft without any reliance on genAI' is a course-structure requirement; P35 (redesign assignments around AI), must, instructors.
units.anchor: W2 courses must include at least one writing assignment or project

units.why: 'Activities like brainstorming, organizing, and editing ... should not be outsourced to genAI' keeps students as the thinkers of their writing process. P32 (students remain primary problem-solver) fits better than P15 or P21 because it rules out outsourcing thinking steps rather than permitting or banning a use.
units.anchor: they should not be outsourced to genAI.

units.why: 'may be supported through classroom activities and individual conversations' names human support in place of AI for brainstorming, organizing and editing; no listed type covers providing human alternatives, so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: may be supported through classroom activities and individual conversations
units.uncovered_note: Where AI is excluded from the writing process, brainstorming, organizing and editing are supported by classroom activities and conversations with humans.

documents.title: CSCI Common Course Policies (Use of AI section)
documents.stance_why: The section opens 'The use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools and resources is encouraged to enhance learning and understanding' and then adds conditions (attribution, own work), so the stance is encourage.
documents.summary: Computer Science department's common course policy section on AI. It encourages AI for learning, coding, debugging and concepts, with attribution including prompts, own-work and verification duties, and revision of AI text.

units.why: 'The use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools and resources is encouraged to enhance learning and understanding' sets the department's default as welcome and encouraged, P02, unit_stance encourage.
units.anchor: The use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools and resources is encouraged to enhance learning

units.why: 'students must use these tools ethically and responsibly' is a general condition on the encouragement, a principle for responsible use; P56 (framework/principles) fits best, must.
units.anchor: students must use these tools ethically and responsibly

units.why: 'AI can be a powerful aid in coding' explicitly allows AI for coding help, with the following sentence part conditions ('not a substitute for personal effort'). Coded P16 (AI-generated code under stated conditions), may.
units.anchor: AI can be a powerful aid in coding

units.why: 'debugging' is named as a use where AI is a powerful aid, so AI help in debugging is permitted: P13.
units.anchor: powerful aid in coding, debugging

units.why: 'conceptual understanding' is named as a use where AI is an aid; using AI to understand concepts is P12, may.
units.anchor: debugging, and conceptual understanding

units.why: 'it should not be a substitute for personal effort and academic integrity' says AI must not replace the student's own effort; P32 (students stay primary problem-solver) rather than P19 because it speaks of effort and not of submitting AI output.
units.anchor: should not be a substitute for personal effort and academic integrity

units.why: 'Any work submitted must be the student's own' is the ownership rule, P29, must.
units.anchor: Any work submitted must be the student's own.

units.why: 'Plagiarism or reliance on AI to complete assignments without proper understanding will not be tolerated and may result in disciplinary action' classifies improper AI reliance as an integrity matter with disciplinary action. P36 (misconduct) fits; the sanction is not concrete, so not P37.
units.anchor: reliance on AI to complete assignments without proper understanding will not be tolerated

units.why: 'When AI tools are used, proper attribution must be given' requires acknowledging AI use, P24, must.
units.anchor: When AI tools are used, proper attribution must be given.

units.why: 'this should be clearly noted in the submission, including the prompts used' asks that code snippets, solutions or significant assistance be noted along with the prompts. P25 (cite the prompt) is chosen over P24 because of the specific prompt requirement.
units.anchor: clearly noted in the submission, including the prompts used

units.why: 'AI can be a valuable tool for exploring new concepts' endorses AI for learning concepts: P12, may.
units.anchor: AI can be a valuable tool for exploring new concepts

units.why: 'generating ideas' is named as a valued use of AI, i.e. brainstorming: P15, may.
units.anchor: exploring new concepts, generating ideas, and improving coding skills

units.why: 'Students are encouraged to use AI to experiment and learn' is explicit encouragement, P02, encourage.
units.anchor: Students are encouraged to use AI to experiment and learn

units.why: 'they should also strive to understand the underlying principles and logic behind the AI-generated content' asks students to understand what AI produced, which is P30 (be able to explain), should.
units.anchor: strive to understand the underlying principles and logic behind the AI-generated content

units.why: 'AI tools have limitations and may not always provide accurate or optimal solutions' is a warning that AI can be wrong, P31, informs.
units.anchor: AI tools have limitations and may not always provide accurate or optimal solutions

units.why: 'Critical thinking and independent verification of AI-generated content are essential' requires verifying AI output: P31, should.
units.anchor: independent verification of AI-generated content are essential to ensure correctness and understanding

units.why: 'AI tools may be used to create drafts and revise written work' permits AI for prose drafting and revision, a prose-specific rule: P18, may.
units.anchor: AI tools may be used to create drafts and revise written work.

units.why: 'AI-generated text should not be used verbatim' limits submitting AI text as is; P19 (do not have AI produce the work you submit) matches the content, should-not, though in the written-work section.
units.anchor: AI-generated text should not be used verbatim.

units.why: 'Students must critically review, edit, and revise any AI-generated content to ensure it is accurate, coherent' requires review of AI text; P31 (verify and evaluate output), must.
units.anchor: Students must critically review, edit, and revise any AI-generated content

units.why: 'Using AI-generated text without proper revision or personal contribution is unacceptable and will be considered a violation of academic integrity' labels it misconduct: P36, must-not.
units.anchor: will be considered a violation of academic integrity

notes: Coder B. Only the three included documents coded. Provost syllabus examples PDF inaccessible (login). The CSCI page is a department-wide page; only the Use of AI section carries AI policy. Multiple-use sentences were split into several units with different anchors.
